title: Synthetic Sepsis Risk Evaluation Lab
summary: A synthetic-only model evaluation lab that compares a prevalence baseline with a calibrated challenger, exposes calibration and threshold tradeoffs, and keeps patient data outside the public system.
outcome: On the fixed synthetic holdout, the calibrated Extra Trees challenger improves AUROC from 0.5000 to 0.9796 and Brier score from 0.0475 to 0.0228. The dashboard turns those model results into an inspectable threshold tradeoff without presenting them as clinical evidence.

deployment.runtime: Synthetic Flask dashboard on Azure Container Apps

At threshold 0.20, 8.7 of every 100 synthetic rows are marked with sensitivity 0.8667 and positive predictive value 0.5000

Build a source-linked container in GitHub Actions
Run the public demo in a scale-to-zero Azure Container App

operationalTradeoffs: Scale to zero minimizes idle compute but can add a cold start for the first visitor.
The public image uses deterministic synthetic inputs only; MIMIC files, patient-level derivatives, local models, MLflow runs, and SHAP exports remain excluded.
The score endpoint is an educational synthetic surface, not a monitored clinical service or operational alerting system.
The current architecture favors a small inspectable release over load capacity, persistent telemetry, authentication, or uptime guarantees.
disclaimer: Synthetic educational research demo only. It contains no patient data, does not establish clinical validity or utility, does not provide clinical guidance, and must not be used for patient care.

presentation.question: How do you make a risk-model demo useful to reviewers without turning synthetic metrics into a clinical claim?
presentation.answer: Start with the cheapest honest baseline, freeze a holdout, calibrate one reproducible challenger, expose threshold consequences, and keep the public data and deployment boundary visibly synthetic.
presentation.decisionSupported: Whether the calibrated challenger adds enough synthetic evaluation value to justify deeper research, and how an illustrative threshold changes the number and composition of rows marked for review.
presentation.architectureAlt: System architecture separating the public synthetic evaluation, Flask API, dashboard, container release, and scale-to-zero Azure deployment from the ignored local MIMIC research boundary.
presentation.evaluationMode: deterministic synthetic holdout evaluation plus live synthetic-only deployment verification

story.recruiterSummary: Risk-model portfolios often lead with a strong score and leave the harder questions unanswered: compared with what, calibrated how, at what review burden, and on which data boundary? This project makes those questions the product. A reviewer can compare the calibrated challenger with a prevalence baseline, change an illustrative threshold, inspect the resulting workload, and trace every public claim to deterministic synthetic evidence.
story.technicalNarrative: A fixed synthetic generator creates the public cohort, then a seeded stratified split freezes training and holdout rows before fitting. The baseline predicts training prevalence. A single-threaded Extra Trees classifier receives three-fold isotonic calibration inside the training partition, chosen after a fixed-seed XGBoost result proved platform-sensitive. The evaluation command emits aggregate discrimination, calibration, leakage, and threshold evidence as versioned JSON. Flask serves health, synthetic timeline, and strictly validated synthetic-score routes; GitHub Actions tests the release and publishes a source-linked AMD64 image; Azure Container Apps runs that image with zero minimum replicas. MIMIC files and every patient-level derivative remain in an ignored local boundary and never enter the public repository or image.
scalabilityRoadmap: Keep the current public surface small until a real research cohort, external validation plan, and clinical governance owner exist.
If repeated-row workflows are studied, add patient-level temporal evaluation, alert deduplication, cooldown rules, and workload simulation before interpreting alert burden.
If traffic exceeds portfolio review volume, add measured request limits, durable telemetry, cost alerts, and an explicit availability objective before increasing replicas.
Do not connect the demo to clinical systems or care workflows without prospective validation, subgroup analysis, security review, and formal safety governance.
story.executiveSummary: The challenger clearly beats the prevalence-only reference on this fixed synthetic fixture, while the product remains explicit about what that does not prove. At threshold 0.20 it marks 8.7 rows per 100 with 86.7% synthetic sensitivity and 50.0% positive predictive value. That tradeoff is useful for reviewing model behavior, not for selecting a clinical alert threshold.
story.intendedUser: A data-science hiring manager, model reviewer, or technical stakeholder assessing reproducibility, calibration, threshold communication, and public data boundaries.

technologyDecisions.rationale: A single-threaded tree ensemble preserves nonlinear synthetic ranking while producing byte-stable evidence across macOS and Linux.
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The deterministic challenger gives up some synthetic AUPRC but avoids platform-dependent public evidence.

technologyDecisions.rationale: The cheapest credible reference and a pre-fit holdout make improvement and calibration claims interpretable.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Report challenger metrics without a named baseline
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: One small synthetic holdout is easy to reproduce but cannot estimate uncertainty, transportability, or patient-level performance.

technologyDecisions.technology: Native HTML, CSS, and SVG dashboard
technologyDecisions.rationale: The threshold control, timeline, table, and disclosure states need accessible browser primitives more than a charting framework.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Add a component or visualization dependency
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The project owns a small amount of rendering code but keeps the public runtime and interaction model compact.

technologyDecisions.technology: Azure Container Apps with a public GHCR image
technologyDecisions.rationale: A scale-to-zero container provides a verifiable HTTPS demo without a paid registry, database, or always-on replica.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Provision Azure Container Registry and an always-on service
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Cold starts and minimal observation are accepted for a low-traffic portfolio surface.

evidence.label: Synthetic holdout AUROC
evidence.context: Calibrated Extra Trees versus 0.5000 for the prevalence-only baseline on 300 fixed holdout rows.
evidence.method: Seeded row holdout with calibration fitted inside training rows only.
evidence.meaning: The challenger ranks positive synthetic rows well above the constant reference.
evidence.interpretation: Strong synthetic ranking evidence, not clinical discrimination evidence.

evidence.label: Synthetic holdout Brier score
evidence.context: Calibrated challenger versus 0.0475 for the constant 5% prevalence estimate.
evidence.method: Mean squared probability error on the fixed synthetic holdout.
evidence.meaning: The calibrated probabilities improve on the cheapest constant estimate.
evidence.threshold: Must be lower than the 0.0475 baseline.
evidence.interpretation: Better probability accuracy on the disclosed synthetic generator only.

evidence.label: Rows marked at threshold 0.20
evidence.context: 26 of 300 holdout rows, with synthetic sensitivity 0.8667 and positive predictive value 0.5000.
evidence.method: Deterministic threshold sweep over held-out calibrated probabilities.
evidence.meaning: The review-volume consequence of one illustrative cutoff.
evidence.threshold: Illustrative threshold 0.20; no clinical threshold is recommended.
evidence.interpretation: Useful for understanding workload tradeoffs, not staffing or care decisions.

evidence.label: Required responsive and automated accessibility checks
evidence.context: Stakeholder and technical states at 1440 px and 390 px.
evidence.method: Headless browser overflow measurement, automated WCAG checks, and manual keyboard review.
evidence.meaning: The evidence and controls remain reachable on desktop and mobile without detected A or AA violations.
evidence.interpretation: A focused release check, not exhaustive assistive-technology certification.

limitations: Synthetic labels are deterministic functions of same-row features, so the task is easier than real-world prediction.
Rows have no patient, site, subgroup, or temporal structure; the evaluation cannot establish patient-level leakage control or transportability.
The evidence has no confidence intervals, external validation, subgroup analysis, drift study, prospective workflow, or intervention effect.
Threshold counts treat rows independently and do not model repeat alerts, suppression, staffing, or clinical workflow.
The anonymous scale-to-zero demo has no availability objective, authentication, durable telemetry, or clinical monitoring.
No result establishes clinical validity, clinical utility, safety, or suitability for patient care.

bulletCandidates.bullet: Built a platform-stable synthetic model evaluation that compares a calibrated Extra Trees challenger with a prevalence baseline, improving holdout AUROC from 0.5000 to 0.9796 and Brier score from 0.0475 to 0.0228 with versioned calibration and threshold evidence.

Designed leakage-aware feature and release contracts that use availability time, preserve patient-level splitting for local research, reject unsafe public score payloads, and keep MIMIC data, derived rows, models, and explanations outside Git and the deployed image.

Delivered an accessible threshold and timeline dashboard with explicit loading, empty, error, and retry states, verified at 1440 px and 390 px, then released it through green Linux CI to a source-verified scale-to-zero Azure Container App.
